youtube_title: The Christmas Tree Ship: the Rouse Simmons, lost on Lake Michigan in 1912
body: For years after the ship went down, Christmas trees kept washing ashore. On November 22, 1912, the schooner Rouse Simmons left Thompson, Michigan, bound for Chicago, her deck piled high with Christmas trees. Her captain, Herman Schuenemann, was known as Captain Santa. The next afternoon, a life-saving crew at Kewaunee, Wisconsin, spotted a schooner flying a distress signal; a rescue boat from Two Rivers found nothing. Everyone aboard was lost. No one knows exactly how many; estimates run as high as 23. Fishermen pulled evergreens up in their nets, and in the 1920s a fishing net brought up the captain's wallet. The wreck was found in 1971 off Two Rivers. His widow and daughters kept selling Christmas trees in Chicago, and since 2000 a Coast Guard cutter has carried trees to the city every year.
